records.summary: StateProjectResult owns @aurelia/state builder flow, source decorator issues, store lookup issues, and exact raw Error authority rows.
records.rationale: @aurelia/state is plugin-backed framework state, not an ordinary DI state class. Its store configuration starts in StateDefaultConfiguration builder chains, then the framework creating AppTask creates Store instances and registers them with IStoreRegistry. Raw framework Error sites should be modeled with StateIssue products and exact StateRawErrorAuthority links only when semantic-runtime owns the corresponding phase; live DevTools host/lifecycle errors remain intentionally unclaimed.
guidance: Use StateStores for valid StateDefaultConfiguration.init(...) and .withStore(...) builder facts before AppTask execution.

StateStoreConfiguration carries the TypeChecker-projected initial-state argument type so & state binding behavior can evaluate against store.getState() without executing the store, and retains the initial-state source address for static source-value reads of configured initial state.

StateBindingScopeProjector mirrors createStateBindingScope(state, scope): boundary scope, parent is the original template scope, binding context comes from the configured store state type, and dynamic store-name arguments stay open. Binding behaviors use it as an evaluator handoff; state/dispatch commands publish the prepared scope as their instruction expression scope.

RuntimeBindingExpressionScopeProjector spends the same state binding-behavior handoff for binding data-flow and observed dependencies: astBind lets StateBindingBehavior call binding.useScope(...), while astEvaluate later unwraps binding behaviors and evaluates the inner expression against that effective scope. Interpolation holes use the same handoff because runtime-html binds each hole through InterpolationPartBinding before evaluating it.

RuntimeBindingSourceValueEvaluator reads StateBinding scope slots through the configured initial-state source expression when a static source-value consumer needs an actual value; this is initial-state reduction, not action/lifecycle emulation.

Use StateIssues for builder/store-registry raw Error rows: withStore after registration, reserved default store names, duplicate store registration, missing named-store lookup, and invalid @fromState(...) target contexts.

FromStateDecoratorBindingSite is the valid decorator source handoff for positive StateGetterBinding materialization. StateGetterBindingMaterializationProjectPass spends it into state-getter-bindings rows with store resolution, selector return type, and target member type projection.
State store lookup issues are post-template because state/dispatch binding commands and & state:'name' binding behaviors are visible only after template runtime products and expression parses exist.

.state and .dispatch commands are full value-site/data-flow surfaces: StateBinding exposes store-state reads into target access/value-channel flow, and StateDispatchBinding exposes event listener target operations plus state-dispatch-action source operations/value channels.

State-dispatch payload expressions reuse template listener event-scope typing: $event.currentTarget is refined from the authored host element, and native value-bearing form controls refine $event.target through the same DOM tag-name-map substrate as observer lookup.

The state-store list authoring recipe now verifies store-backed .state, .dispatch, & state, and interpolation-part data flow plus observed dependencies for store-scope reads such as title, label, collection rows, draft === "", and $event.target.value; dispatch value-channel payloads should preserve known action type literals while refining form-control event target values.

Framework corpus accepts state-store/store as query aliases for the stored state concept, so @aurelia/state route pressure can use plugin-specific vocabulary without splitting the corpus concept ontology.
Remaining state-command pressure is dynamic store-name selection, broader non-form event-target policy, and a future policy for action payload target types, not basic command value-flow admission.

Remaining @fromState pressure is the bridge from source/store/type StateGetterBinding products into controller-owned runtime binding publication, target update operations, and connectable observed-dependency rows.
Keep @fromState(...) target validation source-owned, not observation-owned; the shared decorator-target helper lives under type-system for this reason.
Leave DevTools dispatch errors to runtime host/lifecycle substrates; semantic-runtime does not model browser extension availability or live DevTools message payloads.

anchors.summary: Materializes @aurelia/state store configuration, initial state type, and issue products.
Projects & state binding behavior and state/dispatch command expressions into store-backed binding scopes.
Projects binding-behavior bind-time scope handoffs for data-flow and observed-dependency source reads.
Materializes named-store lookup failures from @fromState(...), state/dispatch binding commands, and state binding behavior arguments.
Valid @fromState field/setter decorator source site that preserves store-name, selector, and target member spans.
Materializes positive StateGetterBinding products from @fromState decorator sites with store and TypeChecker projection.
Public state-getter-bindings API projection for @fromState-created StateGetterBinding products.
Materializes source-order failures where StateDefaultConfiguration.withStore(...) follows registration of the same config object.
Verify exact used raw Error references for @aurelia/state.

records.summary: State store configuration must spend DI registration and resolver-container ownership before compiler worlds, controller bindings, types, and diagnostics select visible stores.
records.rationale: The bounded plugin-capability pass found that semantic-runtime already retains exact default/named store configuration, DI registration operations, resolver lookup owners, compiler consulting containers, and runtime controller frames, but drops the ownership join before state materialization. Builder mutations are scanned and names are grouped project-wide, then the global store array feeds every expression world, template state scope, @fromState binding, and missing-store diagnostic. Two roots with same-named incompatible stores can therefore leak types, produce false duplicates, or suppress missing-store diagnostics. The repair is an ownership reconnection, not deeper reducer/effect execution.
guidance: Do not patch individual state queries with app-root or source-file filters. AppRoot is a selection context, while container admission, inheritance, and shadowing determine persistent visibility.

Preserve exact evaluator configuration-value origin on ConfigurationStepObservation so StateDefaultConfiguration.init(...) and .withStore(...) values can join to the registration operation that admitted the configuration.

Materialize StateStoreConfiguration from admitted ContainerRegistrationOperation rows and retain the registration operation and receiving container. Select visible stores through the effective IStoreRegistry resolver owner for the consulting compiler or runtime controller container.

Use one selector for expression worlds, state binding scopes, state/dispatch commands, & state, @fromState, and store lookup diagnostics. Arbitrary user IStoreRegistry providers make absence open rather than confidently missing.

Split source recognition of @fromState from controller-applied StateGetterBinding publication. RuntimeControllerFrame is the applied owner, matching the existing WatchDefinition to RuntimeWatcher to RuntimeControllerFrame precedent.
Keep the public StateStores query project-wide, but expose operation/container/definition/controller ownership so IDE, MCP, and future AOT consumers can select an honest cohort.

Before implementation, add pressure with two admitted roots that define conflicting same-named stores, parent-container inheritance, child shadowing, and custom-registry openness. Reducers, effects, middleware, transitions, subscriptions, and asynchronous dispatch remain outside this frontier.
